newsitem.title: FINLAND: AMER HITS NEW YEAR-HIGH ON OWNERSHIP DEAL.
newsitem.headline: AMER HITS NEW YEAR-HIGH ON OWNERSHIP DEAL.

text.p: Shares in Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma resumed trade with sharp gains after a suspension on Monday as its K-shareholders said they planned to sell a majority to Briton Jonathan Bryan Guinness, Lord Moyne.
At 1650/1350 GMT, Amer traded at 108 markka, up nearly seven percent, after earlier peaking at 116.10 markka: its last year-high was 110 markka on February 21.

One analyst said a key reason for enthusiasm for the deal would be Moyne's experience in branding and marketing -- the British investor is a former employee of brewer Guinness Plc, although this deal was unconnected with that company.
"I think especially when you take the longer-term view it would be more positive for the company," he said.
It would benefit Amer to have owners whose main aim is business, as opposed to the less focussed approach of Amer's current diverse Finnish institutional K-shareholders, he added.
But short-term, analysts agreed the company faces a major challenge especially in boosting its market share in U.S. golf equipment markets.
"If (Moyne) intends to make a profit he must be able to increase (Amer's) market share in golf," said Jukka Fransas, analyst at FSB Securities, retaining a neutral stance on the stock.
